title: Kolkata put under heavy rain warning as Akvan nears; very heavy rain for coastal Bengal
dek: Kolkata's weather office now forecasts heavy rain in the city on Thursday and Friday and 7-20 cm at isolated places in South 24 Parganas and East Midnapore from Thursday; fishermen are told to stay ashore until Friday.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Kolkata, Howrah, Hooghly and North 24 Parganas are now under a heavy rain warning for Thursday and Friday as Severe Cyclonic Storm Akvan nears the coast, the Regional Meteorological Centre (RMC) in Kolkata said in its 11.30 am special bulletin on Thursday, and heavy to very heavy rain of 7-20 cm is now forecast for South 24 Parganas and East Midnapore from Thursday rather than only on Friday. On Friday the very heavy rain spreads to West Midnapore, Jhargram and Bankura.

The upgrade follows the storm's faster movement north overnight. At 5.30 am on Thursday it lay about 590 km south of Puri, moving at 12 kmph, and the India Meteorological Department (IMD) expects it to cross the coast between Narsapur in Andhra Pradesh and Puri in Odisha, close to Gopalpur, around noon on Friday, before weakening over Odisha. Light to moderate rain fell across Kolkata and several south Bengal districts from Thursday morning, according to reports. The RMC has raised the signal at the Kolkata and Haldia ports to local cautionary signal No. 3 and has told fishermen not to go out along and off the Bengal coast until Friday.

## Latest forecast

Until 8.30 am on Friday, the RMC forecasts light to moderate rain at most places in Kolkata, Howrah, Hooghly, the two 24 Parganas, the two Midnapores and Jhargram, with heavy to very heavy falls at one or two places in South 24 Parganas and East Midnapore and heavy rain of 7-11 cm at one or two places in Kolkata, Howrah, Hooghly, North 24 Parganas, West Midnapore and Jhargram. Thunderstorms with gusts of 40-50 kmph are likely at one or two places in South 24 Parganas and East Midnapore, and of 30-40 kmph elsewhere in south Bengal.

From Friday morning to Saturday morning, rain is very likely at most places in every south Bengal district. The RMC forecasts heavy to very heavy rain at one or two places in South 24 Parganas, East and West Midnapore, Jhargram and Bankura, and heavy rain in Howrah, Hooghly, Kolkata, North 24 Parganas and Purulia. As the storm's remnants move inland on Saturday, heavy rain is likely at one or two places in Murshidabad. Light rain is expected on Sunday and Monday, and dry weather across south Bengal from Tuesday, 24 November.

The RMC warned of lightning strikes, especially in open fields, temporary waterlogging in low-lying areas and underpasses on Thursday and Friday, some damage to standing crops and horticulture, and damage to kutcha roads and vulnerable kutcha houses, including the possibility of walls collapsing. It advised people not to shelter under trees or electric poles, to keep harvested paddy in a safe place, and said beach activities and traffic should be regulated on Thursday and Friday.

North Bengal is expected to get light to moderate rain at a few places from Thursday to Saturday, with thunderstorms and gusts of 30-40 kmph at one or two places in Malda and the two Dinajpurs, before turning dry from 24 November.

## At sea

Squally winds of 40-50 kmph gusting to 60 kmph are expected along and off the West Bengal coast on Thursday and Friday, with very rough to high seas, the RMC said. Over the north-west Bay of Bengal, winds are expected to strengthen to gale force, 70-80 kmph gusting to 90 kmph, until Friday noon. Fishermen have been told not to venture into the sea along the Bengal coast or into the north-west and west-central Bay until 20 November. The warnings matter for the trawler fleets of Digha, Kakdwip, Namkhana and Frasergunj, which work these waters, and the signal at Sagar Island has been raised to sectional signal No. II.

## Why it matters for Bengal

Rain in the second half of November comes as the aman paddy crop, south Bengal's main rice crop, approaches harvest, and as potato planting begins in districts such as Hooghly and Paschim Medinipur; heavy rain at this stage can flatten ripe paddy and waterlog fields. Bengal escaped the worst of Cyclone Arnab and Cyclone Murasu, which hit Andhra Pradesh and Odisha in late October and early November. In Odisha, about 47,000 people had been evacuated by Thursday morning ahead of Akvan's landfall.

## What happens next

The RMC in Kolkata updates its special bulletins as the storm moves, and the IMD issues national bulletins every three hours. The heaviest rain for south Bengal is forecast for Friday and Friday night. The Declaration will update this story as forecasts for Bengal are revised.
